subject: Decision sprint: scope, success criteria and proposed probe suite
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medivista.com>, Mark Davenport <mark.davenport@medivista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision sprint: scope, success criteria and proposed probe suite

Hi Elena / Mark —

Thanks for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align the bake-off window and decision sprint: 

Top pain points you reiterated:
- 95th-pctl latency spikes during peak-hours (current infra) causing UI dropouts
- Unpredictable per-token cost when usage scales beyond pilot
- Data residency + auditability for PHI-sensitive logs

Stated goals for the pilot / decision sprint (what success looks like):
1) Latency: 95th pctl <= 600ms for 8K-context LLM under realistic user mix
2) Cost: predictable per-inference cost within 20% of forecasted model/usage profile
3) Reliability: graceful degradation (fallback to smaller variant) with <1% error rate during stress tests
4) Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and retention controls in place for trial data

Proposed probe suite (things we should run during the 10-day POC):
- Throughput parity probe: sustained 100 req/s mixed prompt lengths for 2 hours (measure avg & 95th latency)
- Token-cost replay: run 48-hour historical token trace to compare billed tokens vs expected cost
- Cold/KV cache warmup: 10k-user prefix patterns to validate KV cache hit curve and latency ramp
- Multi-region failover: simulate us-west outage and validate routing/fallback to us-east within 30s
- Security/compliance checklist: provide SOC2 snapshot + demo of audit log export

Owners & rough timeline suggestion:
- Redwood test harness & baseline: Marissa (SE) — propose week of Apr 12 for lab runs
- Integration + token-trace replay: Jonas (product infra) — needs the CSV trace from your side
- Procurement & SOC2 artifacts: Avery — will coordinate with your security lead

Attachments: I’m attaching a lightweight bake-off checklist and a suggested priority matrix (MediVista-priority-matrix.xlsx). Please review and flag anything we missed.

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm priority ordering for the success criteria (latency vs cost vs compliance) — this will change schedule/variants we select
2) Share the 48-hour token trace (or a sample) by EOD Apr 8 so Jonas can scope replay
3) Confirm whether procurement wants an NDA or MSA first (we can fast-track a short SOW)

If that all looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Apr 11 to align engineers and lock in the test window.

Thanks —
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 10:12 AM Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap from our side...

Avery — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Priority ordering: reliability (95th pctl) is top, then compliance, then cost. If you can show that latency spikes are mitigated under peak, we’ll be comfortable with cost tradeoffs during the POC.
2) Token trace: we can extract a 48-hour anonymized trace but will need a small CYA redaction step — Mark will send the file by EOD Apr 8.
3) Procurement path: our procurement/legal asks for a short SOW and SOC2 evidence first; NDA is already in place. Please send SOC2 artifact checklist and the SOW template.

We’re available for an Apr 11 kickoff in the afternoon (after 1pm PT).

Cheers,
Elena Torres
Director, Product Ops — MediVista Health
elena.torres@medivista.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

P.S. Can you also include a short one-pager on degradation/fallback behavior? Our UX lead wants to see exact UX behavior if model variants are swapped mid-session.

Following up with an internal runbook and proposed slots. I'll own the lab-side test execution and reporting. High-level plan: 

Lab run plan (Marissa):
- Apr 12: baseline runs (single-region, cold cache); measure avg/95th for 8K-context workload
- Apr 13: sustained throughput run (100 req/s, 2h), collect traces + CPU/GPU utilization
- Apr 14: failover simulation and fallback validation (us-west outage)
- Apr 15: token-trace replay (requires the CSV from MediVista)

Data we need from MediVista (owners assigned):
- 48-hour token trace (Mark) — CSV + prompt length distribution by Apr 8
- UX degradation acceptance criteria (Elena) — one-pager by Apr 9
- List of IP allowlists and any IPs for test endpoints (security team)

Deliverables after POC run (we aim to deliver within 48 hours of final test):
- Test report: latency percentiles, throughput graphs, error modes, and cost projection (Jonas)
- SOC2 artifacts packet & audit log demo (Avery)
- Short one-pager on degradation UX with screenshots + suggested UX fallback patterns (Marissa)

Proposed kickoff: Apr 11, 1:30pm PT (30 mins) — if that works I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Note on acceptance gates: if the 95th pctl during throughput run exceeds 900ms we will run an engineered tuning pass (quantization/packing/batching) and re-test once. That effort will be scoped in the test report.

-Marissa
